passkey.title: Passkey Unlock
passkey.info: Passkeys use FIDO2 / WebAuthn with your authenticator (Touch ID, Windows Hello, YubiKey, etc.) to unlock the vault. When your authenticator supports the PRF extension the vault key is cryptographically derived on-device and no secret is stored. On older authenticators a device-bound gate is used instead—a seal key is stored locally and only released after a verified assertion. Registration auto-detects which mode your authenticator supports.

app.about.tagline: Your codes. Your device. Always secure.
app.about.description: Kemlock keeps your OTP tokens and backup recovery codes safely encrypted on your device — no cloud, no telemetry, no account required.
app.about.features.title: Features
app.about.feature.offline.desc: Your vault stays on your device. The app goes online only to sync with your own server if you turn sync on, and to check a new master password for leaks or update the list of breaches if you turn those on.
app.about.feature.encrypted.desc: Your vault is encrypted with your master password using AES-256-GCM and an scrypt-derived key.
app.about.feature.biometric.desc: Use your fingerprint or face ID to quickly unlock your vault without typing your password.
app.about.feature.qr.desc: Back up your vault or migrate to a new device by scanning QR codes — no cables required.
app.about.privacy.title: Privacy First
app.about.privacy.body: No analytics, no tracking, no accounts. Your vault leaves your device only encrypted, and only for an export or a server you chose.
app.about.storage.title: Local Storage Only
app.about.storage.body: Everything is stored in your device's secure local storage. Uninstalling the app permanently removes all data.
app.about.postquantum.title: Post-Quantum Ready
app.about.postquantum.body: Passkey vault keys are wrapped using ML-KEM (Kyber), a NIST-standardised post-quantum key encapsulation algorithm, making your vault resilient against future quantum computer attacks.

app.privacy.intro: Kemlock is designed with privacy as a core principle. This policy explains what data we do — and do not — collect.
app.privacy.s1.title: 1. No Data Collection
app.privacy.s1.body: Kemlock has no servers and no accounts. No email address or phone number is needed, and nothing you store in the app is sent to the developer.
app.privacy.s2.title: 2. Local Storage Only
app.privacy.s2.body: All information — including your OTP secrets, backup codes, and encrypted vault — is stored on your device. It leaves your device only when you export it, or when you turn on sync or a shared space: then the vault is encrypted on the device and the ciphertext goes to the WebDAV server you chose, never to the developer. If you turn on the password leak check, five characters of a fingerprint (the SHA-1 hash) of the master password you are choosing go to Have I Been Pwned, which also sees your IP address; the password itself never leaves your device. If you turn on updates of the breach list, the app asks Have I Been Pwned for its public list of breaches, at most once a day; the request is the same from every phone and carries nothing from your vault.
app.privacy.s3.title: 3. No Purchases
app.privacy.s3.body: Kemlock is free and open source software under the GPLv3 and sells nothing: it holds no purchase library and sends nothing to any purchase service. The app contains no advertising, crash-reporting or analytics SDKs.
app.privacy.s4.title: 4. No Analytics or Tracking
app.privacy.s4.body: No usage analytics, crash reports, or behavioural tracking of any kind are collected. Your interactions with the app are entirely private and never monitored.
app.privacy.s5.title: 5. Your Control
app.privacy.s5.body: You have full control over your data at all times. You may export, delete, or transfer your vault whenever you choose. Uninstalling the application permanently and irreversibly deletes all stored data from your device.

unlockMethod.removed.shared: {name} no longer opens this vault, but the keys still here share the secret it gave. With a copy made while it opened the vault and its PIN, that secret opens the copies made later too. If {name} was lost or stolen, the sure way is to remove every key, replace the key pair, then add again the keys you still have.
unlockMethod.restart.title: Remove every key?
unlockMethod.restart.body: No key will open this vault until you add one again; until then it opens with its password.
unlockMethod.restart.body.key: No key will open this vault until you add one again; until then it opens with a password, which you choose next.
unlockMethod.restart.done: Every key is removed. Replace the key pair now, then add again the keys you still have: they’ll share a new secret.
unlockMethod.restart.done.mode: Every key is removed, and the vault opens with its password for now. Replace the key pair, then tap Continue to add again the keys you still have: they’ll share a new secret.
unlockMethod.refusal.lastKey: This vault needs a key, so its last one can’t be removed. Choose Password first.
unlockMethod.refusal.safetyNet: That would leave a vault that needs its key with one key and no Recovery Kit. Make a Recovery Kit or add another key first.
unlockMethod.missing: The key is added, and the vault still opens as before. Make a Recovery Kit or add a second key, and the new way of opening is turned on.
unlockMethod.notPinBound: One of this vault’s keys gives its secret on a touch, without its PIN, so it can’t be the vault’s only lock. Password and security key works with it.
unlockMethod.hiddenKeyOnly: A hidden vault opens with its password, or with its password and a key, never with a key alone.
unlockMethod.biometric: Biometric unlock goes off for this vault: it would open the vault without the key.
unlockMethod.autofill: AutoFill keeps a copy of this vault’s codes that opens with the phone’s biometrics, without the key.
unlockMethod.unavailable.iphone: Opening a vault with a security key isn’t available on iPhone yet.
unlockMethod.unavailable.ipad: An iPad has no NFC reader for apps, so it can’t read what opens a vault from a key.

replaceKey.title: Replace vault key
replaceKey.body: Kemlock gives this vault a new key and seals everything in it to that key again. A copy of the old key, such as one in an old phone backup, then opens nothing the vault holds from now on. Your master password stays the same.
replaceKey.kitNote: Your Recovery Kit goes with the old key. You’ll make a new one of the same shape before anything changes, or go on without one.
replaceKey.exposed: Biometric unlock once kept this vault’s key in the app’s storage, beside what opens it, so phone backups made then hold it. A new key keeps them out of what the vault holds from now on.
replaceKey.working: Sealing everything to the new key…
replaceKey.error.incorrect: That password doesn’t open this vault.
replaceKey.error.failed: Couldn’t replace the key. The vault opens as before; try again.
replaceKey.error.unreadable: The key was replaced, but some of what the vault holds couldn’t be read with either key, so it was left as it was. Everything else is sealed to the new key.
replaceKey.kit.title: A new Recovery Kit
replaceKey.kit.body: An old backup holds the Recovery Kit’s key too, so the kit is replaced with the vault’s key. Make a new kit now, split as the old one was; the old pieces stop opening the vault once the key is replaced. Without a kit, a forgotten password means a reset.
replaceKey.done.title: The vault has a new key
replaceKey.done.body: What the vault holds from now on is sealed to the new key. An old phone backup still holds what was in the vault when it was made:
replaceKey.done.nothing: What the vault holds from now on is sealed to the new key. It holds nothing yet that an old phone backup could give away.
replaceKey.done.codes: The secrets of your codes. Set up two-factor authentication again, starting with the accounts that matter most, such as email and banking.
replaceKey.done.backupCodes: Your backup codes. Make new ones where the service lets you.
replaceKey.done.keys: Your keys. Replace them on the servers and services they open.
replaceKey.done.passkeys: Your passkeys. Make new ones with each service, and remove the old ones there.
replaceKey.done.notes: What your notes say, and the files attached to them.
replaceKey.done.webdav: Your WebDAV password and sync passphrase. Change the password on the server, then turn sync off and on again with a new passphrase.
replaceKey.done.spaces: The keys of your shared spaces. Whoever runs a space can make a new one and invite everyone again.
replaceKey.done.vaultwarden: Your Vaultwarden sign-in. Change the account’s master password and sign out its other sessions.
replaceKey.done.exports: Your old Recovery Kit. Exports made while it existed still open with their password and with its pieces: make a new export, and delete the old ones.

autofill.body: When an app or website asks for a code, Kemlock suggests it above the keyboard. Confirm with {label} and it’s typed in, without opening Kemlock.
autofill.names.detail: Service names and websites stay on this phone, outside the vault, so a suggestion can say GitHub before you confirm. Never email addresses or secrets.
autofill.privacy: This vault’s TOTP and Steam codes are copied for AutoFill, encrypted to a key only this phone’s secure hardware holds, which opens only with {label}. HOTP codes aren’t filled. Turning this off deletes the copy.
autofill.passwords.detail: On the sites and apps each login names
autofill.passwordSaving.detail: After you sign up, or change a password
autofill.passwords.fillOnly: This iPhone fills your logins. Suggesting and saving passwords from Kemlock need iOS 26.2 or later.
autofill.passwords.kept: This vault’s logins are copied for AutoFill, encrypted to a key only this phone’s secure hardware holds, which opens with {label}. Websites and usernames stay on this phone outside the vault, so a suggestion can say ada@example.org before you confirm. A login saved while the vault is locked waits, encrypted, until you open it. Turning this off deletes the copy.
autofill.passkeys.detail: Save the passkeys sites and apps make to this vault, and sign in with them
autofill.passkeys.kept: While this is on, the phone keeps a copy of this vault’s passkeys outside the vault, encrypted to a key only {label} opens, with the sites and account names they belong to, so it can offer them when you sign in. A passkey made while the vault is locked waits, encrypted, until you open it.
autofill.passkeys.assetLinks: When an app asks for a passkey, Kemlock first checks with the site, over the internet, that the app is the site’s own. Browsers are checked against a list of trusted browsers kept in the app.

autofill.passkeys.unsupported.android: Passkeys from Kemlock need Android 14 or later.

autofill.passkeys.on: The phone saves passkeys to this vault and offers them when you sign in.

securityKeys.openpgp.error.otherCard: This security key isn’t the one shown, or its PGP keys changed since. Nothing was changed on it.
securityKeys.openpgp.pin.body: Type the PIN of the PGP keys on this security key. Kemlock keeps it only while the key is connected.
securityKeys.openpgp.pin.hint: A new key’s PIN is 123456 and its admin PIN is 12345678.
securityKeys.openpgp.pin.lastTry: A wrong PIN now blocks it.
securityKeys.openpgp.use.title: Use your security key
securityKeys.openpgp.use.decrypt: {name} opens the message on your security key.
securityKeys.openpgp.use.wrongCard: This security key doesn’t hold {name}. Use the one with serial number {serial}.
securityKeys.openpgp.use.otherCard: This security key doesn’t hold {name}. Use the one it was put on.
securityKeys.openpgp.use.badSignature: The security key didn’t sign correctly, so nothing was signed.
securityKeys.openpgp.use.blocked: The PIN of this security key is blocked. The admin PIN or the reset code unblocks it.
securityKeys.openpgp.everySignature: Ask for the PIN for every signature
securityKeys.openpgp.allBlocked: The PIN and the admin PIN are blocked and no reset code is left, so the keys on this card can no longer be used. Only a factory reset of its PGP keys remains.
securityKeys.openpgp.takenAway: The key was taken away before it answered. Kemlock doesn’t know whether it took the new code: try the new one, then the old one.
securityKeys.openpgp.touch.title: Touch for {place}
securityKeys.openpgp.touch.permanent: Only a factory reset turns it off
securityKeys.openpgp.touch.permanent.bod: The key will then ask for a touch this way for as long as it has these PGP keys. Only a factory reset of its PGP keys removes it.
securityKeys.openpgp.reset.title: Reset this key’s PGP keys?
securityKeys.openpgp.reset.body: This erases the PGP keys on this security key for good, and its PIN goes back to 123456 and its admin PIN to 12345678. Its passkeys and codes stay. A key made on it can’t be got back; the vault keeps its public half.
securityKeys.openpgp.add.title: Add to vault
securityKeys.openpgp.add.body: The vault keeps the public key of the card’s keys, and never a secret. Add it from a copy you have, or have the card make one.
securityKeys.openpgp.add.import: Use a public key you have
securityKeys.openpgp.add.import.detail: Paste it: one of its keys must be on this card
securityKeys.openpgp.add.make.detail: With a name and email, signed by the card
securityKeys.openpgp.add.notThisCard: This public key isn’t this card’s key: none of its keys is on the card.
securityKeys.openpgp.add.unreadable: This isn’t a public key Kemlock can read.
securityKeys.openpgp.add.make.note: The card signs a new public key for this name and email. It differs from one you may have published before.
securityKeys.openpgp.generate.title: Generate keys on this key
securityKeys.openpgp.generate.usbOnly: Plug the key in to generate RSA keys of this size.
securityKeys.openpgp.generate.noBackup: These keys will exist only on this security key: they can’t be backed up, and losing the key loses them.
securityKeys.openpgp.generate.none: This card offers no kind of key Kemlock can use.
securityKeys.openpgp.generate.replace.ti: Replace the keys on this key?
securityKeys.openpgp.generate.replace.bo: The keys now on this security key will be destroyed, and whatever only they open stays closed.
securityKeys.openpgp.generate.incomplete: The key was taken away before its new keys were set up, so they are incomplete and nothing was added to the vault. Present it again and finish setting up, or generate again.
securityKeys.openpgp.move.title: Move a key from the vault
securityKeys.openpgp.move.none: This vault has no PGP key to move: none of its PGP keys holds its private half here.
securityKeys.openpgp.move.cannotHold: This security key can’t hold this key, so nothing will be sent to it.
securityKeys.openpgp.move.keep: Keep a copy in this vault
securityKeys.openpgp.move.warning: Without a copy, this vault can no longer export or restore the key’s private half: only the security key will hold it. Exports and backups made before still hold it, and so do your other devices until they sync.
securityKeys.openpgp.move.incomplete: The move did not complete. The key in this vault is as it was.
securityKeys.openpgp.move.done: {name} is now on the security key.
securityKeys.openpgp.move.copied: {name} is on the security key, and still in this vault.
keyCodes.touch: Needs a touch on the key
keyCodes.readAgo: Read from the key {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} ago.
keyCodes.neverLeave: These secrets never leave the key, so backups list them as “on your key, not in this file”.
keyCodes.stale: Read the key again for a code
keyCodes.counter: Counter-based: ask the key for a code
keyCodes.counter.next: Next code for {name}, from the key
keyCodes.row.read: Read the key for the code of {name}
keyCodes.unsupported: This key keeps no codes Kemlock can read.
keyCodes.interrupted: The read didn’t finish: the key was taken away too soon. Nothing was changed.
keyCodes.interrupted.partial: The read didn’t finish: the key was taken away before its codes were read. Its accounts are listed; read it again for the codes.
keyCodes.notTouched: The key wasn’t touched in time.
keyCodes.otherKey: This isn’t the key that holds this account.
keyCodes.untrusted: This key accepted the password but couldn’t prove that it knows it, so it couldn’t be trusted. Kemlock stopped and listed nothing.
keyCodes.failed: Talking to the key’s code application failed.
keyCodes.noSuchAccount: The key no longer holds this account. Read the key again.
keyCodes.prompt.title: Security key
keyCodes.prompt.present: Hold your key to the phone, or plug it in.
keyCodes.prompt.working: Talking to your key. Keep it in place.
keyCodes.sheet.secret: The secret is on the key and can’t be shown, copied or exported. If you lose the key, these codes are gone: keep the service’s backup codes.
keyCodes.sheet.tagsNote: Tags and the note are kept in this vault, not on the key.
keyCodes.delete.title: Delete this account from the key?
keyCodes.delete.body: {name} will be deleted from the key. Its codes can’t be made again unless you set up two-step login anew with the service.
keyCodes.password.title: Key password
keyCodes.password.body: The codes on this key are protected by a password. It isn’t your vault’s password, and it isn’t what protects your vault.
keyCodes.password.label: Key password
keyCodes.password.remember.detail: Kemlock keeps what proves the password to this one key, encrypted in this vault. It never keeps the password, and never puts it in a backup or in sync.
keyCodes.password.wrong: That password isn’t right. Nothing was listed.
keyCodes.password.refused: The remembered password no longer opens this key, so Kemlock forgot it. Type the key’s password.
keyCodes.password.set.body: Without a password, anyone who holds the key can read its codes. The password protects the codes on the key, not your vault.
keyCodes.password.remove.title: Remove the key’s password?
keyCodes.password.remove.body: Anyone who holds the key will be able to read its codes.
keyCodes.password.wasSet: The key now asks for its password.
keyCodes.password.wasRemoved: The key no longer asks for a password.
keyCodes.move.title: Move this account to your key?
keyCodes.copy.title: Copy this account to your key?
keyCodes.move.body: Kemlock writes the account to the key, checks that the key’s code matches this vault’s, and only then takes it out of this vault.
keyCodes.copy.body: The account stays in this vault and is also written to the key.
keyCodes.move.warning.lost: If you lose the key, these codes are gone. Keep the service’s backup codes.
keyCodes.move.warning.backups: Backups made before today, and your other phones until they sync, still hold the secret.
keyCodes.move.touch: Ask for a touch on the key for each code
keyCodes.moved: {name} is now on your key, and no longer in this vault.
keyCodes.move.mismatch: Not finished: the key’s code didn’t match this vault’s. The account is still in this vault, and what was written to the key was removed.
keyCodes.move.unchecked: Not finished: the key was taken away before its code could be checked. The account is still in this vault.
keyCodes.refused.steam: Security keys can’t hold Steam Guard accounts.
keyCodes.refused.space: An account of a shared space can’t go to a key.
keyCodes.refused.name: This name is too long for the key: {bytes} bytes, and the key takes 64. Shorten the service or account name.
keyCodes.refused.algorithm: This key’s firmware ({version}) can’t hold SHA-512 accounts.
keyCodes.refused.touch: This key’s firmware ({version}) can’t ask for a touch.
keyCodes.refused.secret: This account’s secret or settings can’t be put on a key.
keyCodes.replace.title: Replace the account on the key?
keyCodes.replace.body: The key already holds an account named {name}. Its secret will be replaced.
keyCodes.full: The key is full: a key with this firmware holds {capacity} accounts. Nothing was changed.
keyCodes.keep.detail: The secret goes to the key and is never stored in this vault.
keyCodes.manage.title: Codes on this key
keyCodes.manage.empty: No account of this key is listed yet. Read the key to list them.
keyCodes.erase: Erase every code on this key
keyCodes.erase.title: Erase every code on this key?
keyCodes.erase.body: Every account in the key’s code application is erased, with its password. Passkeys, PGP keys and certificates on the key are untouched. The codes can’t be made again unless you set up two-step login anew with each service.
keyCodes.erased: Every code on the key was erased.
keyCodes.forget: Forget this key in this vault
keyCodes.forget.title: Forget this key in this vault?
keyCodes.forget.body: Kemlock forgets the names of this key’s accounts, their tags and notes, and its remembered password. Nothing is sent to the key: its codes stay on it.
keyCodes.forgotten: The key was forgotten in this vault.
export.onKey: {count, plural, one {# account is} other {# accounts are}} on your key, not in this file
piv.title: Certificates
piv.caption: The key’s smartcard slots (PIV), used to sign in to computers and sign documents.
piv.gone: Present the key again to see its certificates.
piv.slot.9a.purpose: Slot 9a signs you in to computers and networks, after the PIN.
piv.slot.9c.purpose: Slot 9c signs documents and mail, and asks for the PIN before every signature.
piv.slot.9d.purpose: Slot 9d opens mail and files encrypted to you, after the PIN.
piv.slot.9e.purpose: Slot 9e proves the card is there, such as at a door, with no PIN.
piv.slot.needsContact: Plug the key in to read this slot
piv.triesLeft: {count, plural, one {# try left} other {# tries left}}
piv.defaultWarning: Anyone can change this key’s certificates while the management key is the factory default. Change it, and keep the new one in your vault.
piv.codes.bothBlocked: The PIN and the PUK are both blocked: the slots’ keys can no longer be used, and only a reset remains.
piv.codes.factory: {codes, select, pin {The PIN is still the factory one, 123456, which anyone can look up. Change it.} puk {The PUK is still the factory one, 12345678, which anyone can look up. Change it.} other {The PIN and the PUK are still the factory ones, 123456 and 12345678, which anyone can look up. Change them.}}
piv.error.otherKey: This is another key than the one shown. Nothing was changed on it.
piv.error.managementKey: The key didn’t accept that management key.
piv.error.badSignature: The key didn’t sign correctly, so nothing was stored.
piv.error.noRoom: The certificate doesn’t fit on this key. The slot is unchanged.
piv.error.refused: The key refused. Nothing was changed.
piv.lastTry.title: Last try
piv.lastTry.pin: One try is left: a wrong PIN now blocks it, and only the PUK can set a new one.
piv.lastTry.puk: One try is left: a wrong PUK now blocks it, and then only a reset helps.
piv.slot.title: {name} ({slot})
piv.slot.unreadable.body: This slot holds something Kemlock can’t read as a certificate. You can still export it as it is, or replace it.
piv.import.title: Import a certificate
piv.import.privateKey: This is a private key. Kemlock imports certificates only: keys are made on the security key.
piv.import.request: This is a certificate request. Send it to the authority, and import the certificate it sends back.
piv.import.publicKey: This is a public key, not a certificate. Import the certificate that holds it.
piv.import.unreadable: This isn’t a certificate Kemlock can read. Choose a certificate in .crt, .cer, .pem or .der form.
piv.import.mismatch: This certificate is for another key, not the one in this slot. The slot is unchanged.
piv.import.confirm.title: Import into {slot}?
piv.import.confirm.body: It names {name}, and is valid from {from} until {until}.
piv.import.unchecked: Kemlock could not check that this certificate belongs to the slot’s key: this key doesn’t say which key the slot holds.
piv.remove.title: Remove the certificate from {slot}?
piv.remove.body: The slot’s private key stays on the security key, and Kemlock can’t remove it. Computers stop offering it until the slot gets a certificate again.
piv.generate.title: Generate a key
piv.generate.caption: The security key makes a new private key in slot {slot} ({name}), and it never leaves the key.
piv.generate.inUse: This slot holds a key and a certificate now. Generating replaces both, for good.
piv.generate.keyOnly: This slot has a key and no certificate yet. Finish gives that key its certificate.
piv.generate.dropped: The key was taken away after it made the new key and before its certificate was stored. The slot has a new key and no certificate yet: present the key again and tap Finish.
piv.generate.rsaSlow: Making an RSA key takes several seconds: keep the key still until it’s done.
piv.generate.selfSigned.hint: The key signs its own certificate. Enough for most computers and tools.
piv.generate.request.hint: Kemlock writes a request for an authority to sign, and puts a placeholder certificate valid one year in the slot until you import the authority’s.
piv.generate.name: Name on the certificate
piv.generate.nameTooLong: A name has at most 64 characters.
piv.generate.replace.title: Replace the key in {slot}?
piv.generate.replace.body: The key and the certificate in this slot now are replaced. Anything that used them, such as signing in to a computer, stops working with them.
piv.generate.done.request: Key generated, with a placeholder certificate. Send the request to your authority.
piv.pin.about: The PIN lets a computer use the slots’ keys. It has 6 to 8 characters.
piv.puk.about: The PUK sets a new PIN once the PIN is blocked. It has 8 characters.
piv.pin.rules: 6 to 8 characters. Some computers accept digits only.
piv.puk.rules: 8 characters. Some computers accept digits only.
piv.pin.unblock.body: The PIN is blocked. Type the PUK to set a new PIN.
piv.pin.factoryRefused: 123456 is the factory PIN, which anyone can look up. Choose another.
piv.puk.factoryRefused: 12345678 is the factory PUK, which anyone can look up. Choose another.
piv.pin.blocked: The PIN is blocked. Unblock it with the PUK.
piv.puk.blocked: The PUK is blocked: it can no longer unblock the PIN. Only a reset clears it.
piv.pin.unblocked: The PIN is unblocked and set.
piv.pin.factoryWarning: This is still the factory PIN, 123456, which anyone can look up. Change it.
piv.puk.factoryWarning: This is still the factory PUK, 12345678, which anyone can look up. Change it.
piv.managementKey.about: The management key lets a phone or computer generate keys and change certificates on this security key. Using the slots’ keys needs only the PIN.
piv.managementKey.keep.on: Kemlock makes a random key and saves it as a secure note before setting it.
piv.managementKey.keep.off: Kemlock shows you the new key to write down, and keeps nothing.
piv.managementKey.cannot: This key can’t change its management key from Kemlock.
piv.managementKey.changed.kept: The management key is now a new {kind} key, kept in this vault as the note “{title}”.
piv.managementKey.changed.shown: The management key is now the {kind} key you wrote down. Kemlock didn’t keep it.
piv.managementKey.notSaved: The vault couldn’t save the note, so nothing was changed on the key.
piv.managementKey.refused: The key refused the new management key: its management key is as before, and Kemlock kept no note of the new one.
piv.managementKey.dropped: The key was taken away while its management key was being changed. The new key is kept in your vault: try it first, and the old one if the key refuses it.
piv.managementKey.dropped.shown: The key was taken away while its management key was being changed. Try the key you wrote down first, and the old one if the key refuses it.
piv.managementKey.show.title: Write down the new management key
piv.managementKey.show.tripleDes: This key takes only a triple DES management key. Here is a new one: write this one down instead.
piv.managementKey.show.warning: Kemlock won’t keep it. Without it, only a reset can change this key’s certificates again.
piv.managementKey.used.vault: Used the management key from your vault.
piv.managementKey.used.typed: Used the management key you typed.
piv.managementKey.ask.notFound: This vault has no note with this key’s management key, and the key no longer has the factory one. A note may be in another vault.
piv.managementKey.ask.vaultRefused: The management key in your vault no longer matches this key.
piv.managementKey.ask.body: Type or paste the management key, in hex. Spaces don’t matter.
piv.managementKey.invalid: A management key is 32, 48 or 64 hex digits.
piv.note.title: Management key – {name}
piv.reset.lost: Every key and certificate in the four slots is erased for good, and the PIN, the PUK and the management key go back to the factory ones.
piv.reset.kept: The key’s passkeys, codes and other applications aren’t touched. To reset, Kemlock first blocks the PIN and the PUK with wrong codes, as the key asks.
piv.reset.finish.body: A reset was started and not finished. Finishing it erases every key and certificate in the four slots, and puts the codes back to the factory ones.
piv.reset.done: The certificates were reset. The PIN is 123456 again, the PUK 12345678, and the management key the factory one.
piv.reset.note.title: Delete the vault’s note?
piv.reset.note.body: The note “{title}” holds the management key the key had before the reset. It no longer opens anything.
autofill.system.ios: Turn Kemlock on in Settings › General › AutoFill & Passwords, so iOS asks it for codes.
autofill.system.android: Choose Kemlock as the autofill service, so Android asks it for codes. Android uses one at a time: a password manager’s autofill stops while Kemlock is chosen.
autofill.systemOn: The phone fills codes from Kemlock.
autofill.noBiometrics: Set up {label} on this phone first: AutoFill opens its copy of the codes only with biometrics.
autofill.chrome: Chrome fills with its own passwords until you choose “Autofill using another service” in its settings.
autofill.hidden: A hidden vault can’t fill codes: its names in suggestions would show that it’s there.
autofill.unsupported.ios: Filling codes into other apps needs iOS 18 or later.
autofill.unsupported.android: Filling codes and passwords into other apps needs Android 11 or later.
about.credits: Passphrases are made from the EFF’s large word list (eff.org/dice), under CC BY 3.0 US. Which part of a web address a site owns comes from the Public Suffix List (publicsuffix.org), under MPL 2.0. On Android, the password rules of known sites come from Apple’s password-manager-resources, under the MIT licence.

tags.placeholder: Work, Personal… press Enter to add
settings.recovery.hint: Opens the vault if you forget its password
settings.sync.hint: Through your own WebDAV server or Vaultwarden
settings.spaces.hint: Share accounts with family or a team
settings.health.kitNone: None — a forgotten password means a reset
settings.offline.detail: Kemlock makes no network request at all
sync.offline: Offline mode is on. Sync is paused.
sync.offline.setup: Offline mode is on. Turn it off to connect to a server.
sync.offline.invite: You can’t join a space while offline mode is on.
leakCheck.offline: Not checked: offline mode is on.
offline.link.title: Open this in your browser?
offline.link.body: Offline mode is on. Kemlock stays offline, but your browser will go online to open it.
recovery.unlock.title: Open with Recovery Kit
recovery.unlock.body: Add enough pieces of the vault’s Recovery Kit to open it without the password. You’ll choose a new password next.
recovery.unlock.noVault: These pieces don’t open any vault on this device. Check that they all come from its current kit.
recovery.unlock.opened: The Recovery Kit opened your vault. Choose a new master password for it; the kit keeps working with the new password.
recovery.collect.start: Add the pieces one at a time: scan a piece’s QR code, or type in its text.
recovery.collect.progress: {count, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}} of {needed} added
recovery.piece.error.format: That isn’t a Recovery Kit piece. Pieces start with BMCKIT1.
recovery.piece.error.checksum: That piece has a typo. Check it against the printed copy.
recovery.piece.error.otherKit: That piece belongs to a different Recovery Kit.
recovery.kit.title: Recovery Kit
recovery.kit.error: Couldn’t make the Recovery Kit. Please try again.
recovery.kit.status.me: Made {date}. One piece, kept by you, opens this vault without its password.
recovery.kit.status.people: Made {date}. Any {needed} of the {total} pieces open this vault without its password.
recovery.kit.replaceHint: Lost a piece, or no longer trust someone who has one? Make a new kit: the old pieces stop opening this vault. Exports made before still open with them.
recovery.kit.body: A Recovery Kit opens this vault if you forget its master password, and opens the encrypted exports you make from now on. Print it, or hand pieces to people you trust.
recovery.kit.me.body: One piece to print and keep somewhere safe, away from your phone.
recovery.kit.people.body: Split into pieces for family or friends. No single person can open your vault; enough of them together can.
recovery.kit.warning: Anyone with {needed, plural, one {this piece} other {# of the pieces}} can open this vault without your password. Keep {needed, plural, one {it} other {them}} as safe as the password itself.
recovery.kit.pieces.me: Print this piece or write it down, then keep it somewhere safe.
recovery.kit.pieces.people: Print the pieces and give one to each person. Any {needed} of the {total} open your vault.
recovery.kit.withCodes: Add my unused backup codes to the printout
recovery.kit.onceHint: The pieces are only shown now. If you lose them, make a new kit.
recovery.kit.replacement.saved: I’ve printed or written down every piece
recovery.print.title: Kemlock Recovery Kit — piece {index} of {total} · {vault}
recovery.print.meta: Made {date}. Any {needed} of {total} pieces open the vault.
recovery.print.howTo: To use it: on the Kemlock lock screen, tap “Forgotten your password?”, then “Use Recovery Kit”, and scan this code. {needed, plural, one {This piece alone opens the vault, so keep it safe.} other {# pieces are needed.}}
vaults.title: Vaults
vaults.body: Each vault has its own password, accounts and backups. The lock screen lists your vaults, except hidden ones, which open when you type their password.
vaults.hidden.alone: No vault is listed on the lock screen, so it shows only a password field. Type a vault’s password to open it.
vaults.hidden.hint: This vault doesn’t appear on the lock screen. To open it, type its password while any vault is selected.
vaults.new.title: New vault
vaults.new.body: Give it a name and its own password. Only that password opens it.
vaults.field.name: Name
vaults.new.hideHint: A hidden vault opens when you type its password on the lock screen. Nobody looking at the app can tell it exists, but its encrypted data is still on the device.
vaults.created: “{name}” created. Lock the app and choose it to open it.
vaults.created.hidden: “{name}” created. To open it, type its password on the lock screen.
vaults.error.passwordInUse: Another vault on this device uses that password. Choose a different one.
vaults.delete.title: Delete “{name}”?
vaults.delete.body: Every account and backup code in this vault is deleted from this device. Other vaults stay. This can’t be undone.
sync.title: Sync
sync.body: Keep this vault the same on all your devices through a WebDAV folder you control, such as Nextcloud, ownCloud or a Synology NAS. It’s encrypted on the device first, files attached to notes too, so the server only stores ciphertext.
sync.field.urlHelper: The WebDAV address of a folder for Kemlock
sync.field.passwordHelper: Create an app password for Kemlock rather than using your main one
sync.field.passphraseHelper: Use the same passphrase on each device. It encrypts the file and never leaves your devices.
sync.error.shortPassphrase: The sync passphrase must be at least 8 characters.
sync.on.hint: Turning sync off keeps your vault on this device and leaves the encrypted files on the server.
sync.problem.insecure: Use an https:// address. Plain http would send your password unencrypted.
sync.problem.auth: The server didn’t accept the username or app password.
sync.problem.folder: That folder doesn’t exist on the server. Create it first, then try again.
sync.problem.conflict: Another device kept changing the file. Kemlock will try again shortly.
sync.problem.network: Couldn’t reach the server. Check the address and your connection.
sync.problem.networkWeb: Couldn’t reach the server. In a browser, the server must also allow this site (CORS); the iOS and Android apps don’t need that.
sync.problem.server: The server reported an error. Try again later.
sync.problem.key: That passphrase doesn’t open the sync file in this folder.
sync.problem.format: This folder has a file Kemlock can’t use for this. Choose another folder.
sync.problem.address: No Vaultwarden answers at that address. Check it, then try again.
sync.problem.signedOut: Your Vaultwarden session ended, as it does after a password change. Sign in again.
sync.problem.unsupported: This Vaultwarden account uses something Kemlock can’t do yet.
sync.problem.homeMissing: Kemlock’s note is gone from your Vaultwarden, so nothing was synced. Turn sync off, then on again.
sync.problem.modeChanged: Another device changed how Vaultwarden keeps your codes, so nothing was synced.
sync.problem.removals: This sync would remove many entries, so it waits for you.
sync.problem.older: The server gave back an older copy of the sync file than this device already synced, so nothing was synced: entries deleted since would have come back. Kemlock will try again. If you put an older copy back yourself, set this sync up again on this device.
vaultwarden.title: Vaultwarden
vaultwarden.body: Keep this vault in your own Vaultwarden, or another Bitwarden-compatible server. Kemlock talks to it directly; no Kemlock server is involved.
vaultwarden.field.serverHelper: Where you open its web vault, such as https://vault.example.com
vaultwarden.field.passwordHelper: Opens your account’s key once. Kemlock doesn’t keep it.
vaultwarden.apiKey.helper: In the web vault: Settings › Security › Keys › View API key. The master password still opens your account’s key.
vaultwarden.apiKey.use: Sign in with an API key
vaultwarden.step.title: Two-step login
vaultwarden.step.yubikeyHelper: Touch your YubiKey with this field selected.
vaultwarden.step.unsupported: This account’s two-step login is one Kemlock can’t do yet, such as Duo. Sign in with an API key instead.
vaultwarden.cert.title: Untrusted certificate
vaultwarden.cert.body: Your phone doesn’t trust this server’s certificate. If it’s your own server with a self-signed certificate, check that this fingerprint is the one your server shows, then trust it.
vaultwarden.cert.warning: A server that normally works without this should never ask. If yours does, someone may be between your phone and the server: don’t trust this certificate, and try again on another network.
vaultwarden.storage.title: How should Vaultwarden keep your codes?
vaultwarden.storage.sealedBody: Vaultwarden keeps your codes but can’t read them, and neither can anyone who gets into your Vaultwarden. Bitwarden apps show sealed notes. Each device needs a sealing passphrase.
vaultwarden.storage.plainBody: Your codes become ordinary Vaultwarden logins. Bitwarden apps show each code next to its password, and Kemlock can show the password of a login that holds your code.
vaultwarden.storage.plainAgree: I understand that anyone who gets into my Vaultwarden will have my passwords and my 2FA codes.

vaultwarden.lockout: If the two-step code for this Vaultwarden is in Kemlock, keep an encrypted export or the Recovery Kit somewhere else, so a new phone can get back in.
vaultwarden.moveOffer.body: Kemlock Server keeps every kind of entry, never sees a hash of your master password, and can fall back to a second server. Moving changes nothing until you confirm it.

spaces.body: Share accounts, backup codes, keys and notes with family or a team; a note’s files go with it. Passkeys stay in your own vault. Everyone in a space needs access to the same WebDAV folder, such as a shared Nextcloud folder. What you put in a space syncs to everyone in it.

spaces.move.title: Move “{name}” to Kemlock Server?
spaces.move.body: This phone makes the space on Kemlock Server, puts every entry in its “Everyone” collection and checks that they all arrived. You become its Owner. The space keeps its name here. Members who haven’t moved keep working through the WebDAV file, which this phone keeps up to date until you close it. That copy works as WebDAV spaces always have: anyone who holds its key reads everything in it, so it can’t carry restrictions. It closes by itself when a member is removed, when keys are replaced, when you add a second collection, or when a grant hides passwords. Then invite people to the server space by email; this space offers no more WebDAV invites.

It keeps syncing through WebDAV, and you can try again.} keysPending {The space’s keys are being replaced. Try again afterwards.} other {The space couldn’t be moved. spaces.copy.close.title: Close the WebDAV copy of “{name}”?
spaces.copy.close.body: Every phone that moved stops reading and writing the file, and the space goes on only through Kemlock Server. Phones that haven’t moved stop receiving changes. Anyone who still holds the old invite can read the file as it was, but will see nothing new. The file stays in the folder, unchanged, until you delete it.

spaces.merge.title: Merge “{name}” into the space on Kemlock Server?
spaces.merge.body: {owner} owns that space and can read everything this phone puts in it. Merge only if you know them. This phone adds its copy of “{name}” to it once, then stops writing the WebDAV file and syncs through Kemlock Server.
space.bridge.warn.title: This closes the WebDAV copy
space.bridge.warn.body: This space still has a WebDAV copy. A second collection, or a grant that hides passwords, is something the WebDAV file can’t keep, so it closes the copy on every phone: they stop reading and writing the file, and anyone holding the old invite sees nothing new. Close it and go on?
